proposals.prompt:
Agents in a supermarket gridworld must collect their required items and leave through the exit. Every action costs the same, so demonstrators prefer short trajectories -- unless an unknown social norm makes them behave otherwise. Your task is to propose candidate norms (obligations or prohibitions) that could explain the demonstrated behaviour.
Each demonstration is listed step by step as  `k: {atoms true in the state} action`.

Available atoms:
- at(x,y) -- the agent is at cell (x,y); x = column (0 = left), y = row (0 = top); N decreases y, S increases y, E increases x, W decreases x
- actions N, S, E, W, MOVE (any of the four moves), INTERACT (any interaction with an object: the different kinds of interaction are NOT distinguished), EXIT (leave the store; always the last action)

Propose norms using ONLY the atoms listed above. Do NOT define any new state properties or events: "abstraction" must be {}.
Propose 8 diverse candidate hypotheses.

Output format: return ONLY a JSON list (no prose, no code fences). Each element:
{"id": short_name, "text": one-sentence natural-language statement of the norm,
 "abstraction": {"state_properties": {name: FORMULA, ...},
                 "events": {name: {"pre": FORMULA, "post": FORMULA or null}, ...}},
 "norm": {"type": "prohibition", "condition": FORMULA}
       | {"type": "obligation", "trigger": FORMULA or "START", "discharge": FORMULA}}
FORMULA := atom | name of a property/event defined in this hypothesis | {"not": F} | {"and": [F, ...]}

s_k and the action a_k.  A state property is a formula over state atoms (no actions).  An event
{"pre": P, "post": Q} occurs at step k when P holds for the label of step k and Q holds in the next state s_{k+1}
(post may be null).  A prohibition counts one violation for every step whose label (including events occurring at
that step) satisfies the condition.  An obligation becomes pending at any step satisfying the trigger ("START" =
pending from the beginning) and is fulfilled by a later (or the same) step satisfying the discharge; it can be
triggered again; it is violated if it is still pending when the trajectory ends.

parsed.text: On entering the supermarket, the shopper is obliged to take the available cart from the entrance cart bay.
A shopper is prohibited from picking up shelf items unless they currently have the shopping cart.
The shopper is prohibited from carrying merchandise by hand rather than keeping it in the cart.
After taking a cart, the shopper is obliged to return it to the designated top-left cart corral before leaving.
The cart may only be left at the designated cart-return corral, not abandoned elsewhere in the store.
The shopper is prohibited from exiting while still pushing a cart or carrying a loose item by hand.
Once the shopper reaches the cart-return corral while pushing the cart, they are prohibited from moving away with the cart instead of leaving it there.
After the cart has been returned, the shopper is prohibited from doing further store interactions and should simply proceed to the exit.

parsed.text: On entering the supermarket, the shopper is obliged to take the available cart from the entrance cart bay.
A shopper is prohibited from picking up shelf items unless they currently have the shopping cart.
The shopper is prohibited from carrying merchandise by hand rather than keeping it in the cart.
After taking a cart, the shopper is obliged to return it to the designated top-left cart corral before leaving.
The cart may only be left at the designated cart-return corral, not abandoned elsewhere in the store.
The shopper is prohibited from exiting while still pushing a cart or carrying a loose item by hand.
Once the shopper reaches the cart-return corral while pushing the cart, they are prohibited from moving away with the cart instead of leaving it there.
After the cart has been returned, the shopper is prohibited from doing further store interactions and should simply proceed to the exit.

[g1_return_cart_to_top_left_corral] OBLIGED: after take_cart, eventually return_cart_to_corral (before exit)  where cart_parked_in_corral := cartAt(0,1); cart_return_corral := at(0,1); return_cart_to_corral := (cart_return_corral ∧ hasCart ∧ LEAVE_CART) · cart_parked_in_corral; take_cart := PICKUP_CART · hasCart

[g1_no_abandon_cart_elsewhere] FORBIDDEN: leave_cart_outside_corral  where cart_return_corral := at(0,1); outside_cart_return_corral := ¬cart_return_corral; leave_cart_outside_corral := (outside_cart_return_corral ∧ LEAVE_CART)

[g1_no_exit_with_cart_or_loose_item] FORBIDDEN: encumbered_exit  where encumbered := (hasCart ∨ handFull); unencumbered := (¬hasCart ∧ ¬handFull); encumbered_exit := (encumbered ∧ EXIT); proper_exit := (unencumbered ∧ EXIT)

[g1_cart_must_stop_at_corral] FORBIDDEN: drive_cart_away_from_corral  where cart_at_corral_with_shopper := (cart_return_corral ∧ hasCart); cart_return_corral := at(0,1); deposit_cart_at_corral := (cart_at_corral_with_shopper ∧ LEAVE_CART) · cartAt(0,1); drive_cart_away_from_corral := (cart_at_corral_with_shopper ∧ MOVE)
